newsitem.title: PERU: Southern Peru's Jan-Aug output up 28.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Southern Peru's Jan-Aug output up 28.4 percent.

text.p: Copper mine output at Southern Peru Copper Corp reached 203,501 tonnes in the first eight months of the year, up 28.4 percent compared with the same period last year, the government said Friday.

Majority owned by U.S. company ASARCO Inc and Peru's largest copper producer, Southern accounted for 64 percent of Peru's total output in the first eight months, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry's preliminary figures.
These figures were for copper produced at Southern's Cuajone and Toquepala open-pit mines.
Peru's copper production rose 21.4 percent to 316,037 tonnes in the first eight months compared with the same period last year.
The country's higher output was due mainly to increased production at Southern, Cyprus Amax Minerals Co's Cerro Verde open pit and at state-owned mining giant Centromin Peru S.A..

Output in the first eight months at Cyprus's Sociedad Minera Cerro Verde S.A., Peru's third largest copper miner, rose to 27,762 tonnes, up 50.2 percent compared with the same period last year. Cerro Verde was privatized in December 1993.
At Centromin, the fourth largest producer, production jumped to 25,352 tonnes in the first eight months, up 13.3 percent.

Meanwhile, output at the country's second largest producer, Magma Copper Co's Tintaya mine, fell 13.0 percent to 37,389 tonnes. The former state-run Tintaya mine was sold to U.S.-based Magma in November 1994.
Copper is Peru's largest single export earner, accounting for $1.199 billion or 21.5 percent of total Peruvian exports in 1995, according to official figures.
The world's sixth largest copper producer, Peru saw output of the red metal climb 10.8 percent to 404,990 tonnes last year compared with 365,513 tonnes the previous year.
